statements.quote: The study was pre-registered on OSF including hypotheses, power analysis, procedure and analytic approach https://osf.io/2d7fe/overview?view_only=c34f80bd046e4c85aafdee3d2c33a74e.

After consenting, participants were randomly assigned to one of three conditions that varied whether they completed the idea-generation task with or without access to an AI chatbot (please see Figure A1 for representative excerpts from the instructions shown in each condition).
statements.locator: p. 11, Method, Submission Phase; points to Figure A1 on p. 33

statements.quote: Additionally, copy-paste functionality was disabled using JavaScript code embedded in the Qualtrics survey.
statements.locator: p. 11, Method, Submission Phase (software description; no code-release claim)

statements.quote: Each submitter was provided with the following rubric to guide their scoring (See Table A1).
statements.locator: p. 12, Occasions; points to Table A1 on p. 34

statements.quote: Each participant produced five ideas for three objects (brick, bubble wrap, frisbee). For participants in the high-agency and low-agency conditions, the survey was designed such that each object corresponded to one human-AI interaction, with chat data logged using JavaScript.

We note two key deviations from our preregistration. Although the preregistered target number of idea submitters was N = 450 (to attain 95% power with a small effect size), external constraints on recruitment duration resulted in a final sample of N = 150.
statements.locator: p. 14, Data Analysis, Statistical Approach (first preregistration deviation)

statements.quote: Second, upon collection of the data, analysis of participants’ chat-log data indicated that a substantial portion of the participants in the high-agency (N = 12) and low-agency (N = 10) conditions did not comply with the task instructions and were therefore excluded from the final analyses.
statements.locator: p. 14, Data Analysis, Statistical Approach (second preregistration deviation)

statements.quote: Using the lme4 package in R (Bates et al., 2015), for each of the preregistered outcome metrics we fit linear mixed effects models with condition as the fixed effect and participants and objects as random effects.
statements.locator: p. 15, Data Analysis, Statistical Approach (analysis-software description; no code-release claim)

statements.quote: S.H.W. collected and analyzed the data. Y.Y. implemented the chatbot in the survey and analyzed chat-log data.

We developed a simple web application in Vercel which emulated the generic AI chatbot experience (e.g., ChatGPT). The interface was embedded in the Qualtrics survey using Javascript. Participants’ chat interactions with the AI, including message sender (i.e., AI or user), message content, and timestamp, were logged as responses together with other survey data through the Qualtrics API. We used the gpt-3.5 model, with the temperature parameter set to 0.7, in line with other research on ChatGPT for creative tasks (e.g., Ashkinaze et al., 2024).
statements.locator: p. 33, Appendix A, Experimental Platform and Paradigm, Web App and Language Model

statements.quote: The model was given the following system prompt for all interactions with participants: “You are a helpful AI assistant in a chat interface. Be conversational, friendly, and helpful. Keep responses concise but informative.”
statements.locator: p. 33, Appendix A, System Prompt (prompt reproduced in the paper)

statements.quote: Creativity Scoring Rubric, Provided to Both Submitters and Evaluators
statements.locator: p. 34, Appendix A, Table A1 title

statements.quote: Two prominent themes emerged: Direct Asks, which referred to cases where the participant prompted the AI system with the task instructions, and Exploratory, which referred to cases where participants asked the AI system to develop ideas based on a more specific category (see Section B for full definitions, examples, and descriptive data).
statements.locator: p. 38, Appendix B, Additional Results, Behavioral Outcomes; definitions and coding prompt reproduced on pp. 39-41

deposits.notes: Preregistration titled The Role of Mindsets in Creative Ideation with AI, doi:10.17605/osf.io/2d7fe. The printed view-only URL returned HTTP 200. The canonical https://osf.io/2d7fe/overview also returned 200; https://api.osf.io/v2/registrations/2d7fe/ returned 200 without the view-only token and reported public=true, embargoed=false. The registration was dated 2025-10-15; the past embargo_end_date of 2026-06-30 is not a current embargo. https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/2d7fe/files/osfstorage/?view_only=c34f80bd046e4c85aafdee3d2c33a74e returned 200 and one folder. Its recursive listing at https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/2d7fe/files/osfstorage/68eee4fa66c852f7eabdec93/ returned 200 and exactly three PNG instruction files; pagination was exhausted. The registration responses attach these three files to the experimental design question. Downloads https://osf.io/download/y7het/, https://osf.io/download/xfng3/, and https://osf.io/download/sdbq4/ each returned 200; their PNG signatures and byte sizes were checked in memory. The required node-children URL returned 404 because this identifier is a registration; https://api.osf.io/v2/registrations/2d7fe/children/ returned 200 with zero children. The registration files-provider listing returned 200 with OSF Storage only, and /resources/ returned 200 with zero linked resources. The license was confirmed at https://api.osf.io/v2/licenses/563c1cf88c5e4a3877f9e96a/ (200). Contains the analysis plan, recruitment targets, assignment procedure, and condition instructions, but no observed assignment records, scores, or participant idea texts. The API's has_data and has_analytic_code flags are false. Also rediscovered by first-author and earlier-title searches.

Found in the author-supplied data_links field of the public PsyArXiv metadata at https://api.osf.io/v2/preprints/tbvq2_v1/ (HTTP 200; has_data_links='available'), not in the saved PDF or the screening form. The linked GitHub page returned 200. One recursive tree request, https://api.github.com/repos/sarahhannahwu/idea_generation/git/trees/HEAD?recursive=1, returned 200, truncated=false, and commit 019140125ef6fa6419cf3f12b2157e6c12ff5cbf. n_files=66 is the complete repository's blob count, not just the linked subdirectory; the 50 listed paths prioritize S1 analysis files, tables, and figures. No CSV or other full tabular dataset appears anywhere in that tree. The data/ directory contains only five PNG figures. https://api.github.com/repos/sarahhannahwu/idea_generation/releases?per_page=100 returned 200 with no releases. No license file was present; the preprint's CC BY license was not assumed to cover repository code or data. Files were read in memory from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sarahhannahwu/idea_generation/019140125ef6fa6419cf3f12b2157e6c12ff5cbf/; README.md, .gitignore, analyses/iriss.qmd, chat_log.ipynb, clustering.ipynb, tables.Rmd, embeddings.py, idea_sampler.py, and doshi_analysis.py all returned 200 (the README and notebooks are under analyses/iriss/). Crucially, clustering.ipynb cell index 2 retains an HTML/plain-text dataframe preview with ten real rows, indices 0-4 and 2125-2129, each with submitter_id, condition, use, creativity, originality, and usefulness. There are ten distinct submitter IDs across all three arms. The display caption says 2130 rows x 13 columns, but only ten rows are present; rows_checked=10 does not claim retrieval of the other 2120 rows or a count of the analyzed sample. These are rater-output records linked to the idea submitter, not complete per-person records. All three has_* flags refer solely to these visible rows. The source of this preview is the unavailable data/iriss_manual_ratings_metrics.csv. The .gitignore explicitly excludes *.csv. Analyses also require absent iriss.csv, iriss_manual_ratings.csv, iriss_trial_data.csv, pilot_no_first_message.csv, passenger_no_first_message.csv, evaluated_compliant_conversations.csv, evaluated_compliant_ideas.csv, and doshi_centroid_analysis.csv. analyses/iriss.qmd lines 80-82 identify the IRiSS sample and C&C '26 poster analyses, supporting relevance to S1. It includes filtering and condition recoding, but cannot be rerun without its inputs. The clustering notebook also includes aggregate summaries and selected idea examples, plus a distinct CloudResearch dataset preview (ten displayed rows from a reported 5265-row dataframe), which was not attributed to S1. chat_log.ipynb shows 45 ResponseId rows with truncated chat strings but no arms or creativity scores; its correspondence to S1 could not be established. Thus this deposit exposes genuine row-level fragments, analysis code and aggregate outputs, but not a complete, usable S1 dataset.

Identified as the source project by the preregistration's registered_from relation, the preprint's node relation, and DataCite's IsVersionOf relation. The public-facing URL returned HTTP 200 but only a generic OSF JavaScript application shell. The authoritative metadata request https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/na8kp/ returned HTTP 401 with 'Authentication credentials were not provided.' No project content, file count, license, or data availability could be confirmed. An account alone may not confer access; project authorization may also be required. No login, access request, or attempt to retrieve protected files was made. The public preregistration and public GitHub repository are separate locations.

notes: Checked 2026-10-09 using Python urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 and no personal identifier. Read all 800 lines of the saved markdown, including references and Appendices A and B through p. 42; verified relevant wording against PDF text using PyMuPDF. Quotations preserve source characters and normalize PDF line breaks to spaces. The saved source is PsyArXiv tbvq2_v1, a 42-page manuscript marked UNDER PEER REVIEW; its SHA-256, 526ad4951a53bbfbbe5c505233f8d3ee59c32f88dd8cd98e4534643735abc3e6, matches OSF's primary-file metadata. Its PDF contains one study-related repository link, the OSF preregistration on p. 10, but no explicit data/code release statement or offer of data on request. The statements inventory also records internal materials pointers, descriptions of software/data handling, and preregistration deviations; these are not claims that raw data were released. forms/c132.json data_and_code has empty data_url and code_url. The public preprint landing page https://osf.io/preprints/psyarxiv/tbvq2_v1/ and metadata endpoint both returned 200. Its files-provider and OSF Storage listings returned 200 and showed one file only, The_role_of_human_agency_in_human_AI_collaborative_creativity.pdf (1668455 bytes); no supplementary data file was listed. Its author-supplied data link led to the GitHub deposit recorded above. The manuscript-only preprint is recorded here as a discovery source, not counted as a separate data/materials deposit. The publisher landing page https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3803784.3816857 returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' bot check; no bypass was attempted and publisher supplementary files or differences from the version of record could not be inspected. Repository links in the bibliography concern other studies: the malformed https://doi.org/https://osf.io/xm2f5_v3 (p. 26) returned 400, and https://doi.org/10.31234/osf.io/yqb29 (p. 27) returned 200, redirecting to https://osf.io/yqb29_v1; neither is a c132 deposit. Public_partial reflects the ten linked rater-output rows retained in a notebook, not availability of the underlying 2130-row dataframe. The fragments do not contain all outputs or ratings for any verified complete S1 sample and lack the full assignment and exclusion records. They cannot establish the full-study per-person means, arm SDs/SEs, randomized/analyzed counts, trials retained per arm, or reproducible diversity measures; they cannot resolve the missing-statistics items in final.open_items. Code offers leads on filtering, centroid calculations, and clustering, but without its source datasets and a version matched to the paper it cannot settle the reported statistical discrepancies. Confidence is medium because the public fragment and missing repository inputs are directly verified, while the OSF source project and ACM version remain inaccessible.

corrections.basis: Both posted-data analysts (analysis/c132/A.json and B.json, 2026-10-10) found no participant, rating, or idea data in the downloaded repository: its only file with a data extension is requirements.txt, and its .gitignore excludes *.csv, so the inputs that analyses/iriss.qmd and tables.Rmd read (compliant_trials_demographics.csv, iriss.csv, iriss_manual_ratings.csv) are absent. The ten rater-output rows seen in a notebook's printed output are a display, not a dataset; nothing could be computed.

No public deposit holds this paper's data: the GitHub repository is code only (see the correction above), the OSF preregistration holds three instruction images, and the OSF project na8kp needs an account.
